class TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::BaseClient
  class RecordRateLimit < Faraday::Middleware
def on_complete(env)
      headers = env.response.headers
      remaining = Integer(headers['X-RateLimit-Remaining'], exception: false)
      reset_at = Integer(headers['X-RateLimit-Reset'], exception: false)
      return if remaining.nil? && reset_at.nil?

      path = env.url.path.delete_prefix(@api_root_path).delete_prefix('/')
      tags = {vendor: @vendor, group: @rate_limit_group_of.call(path)}
      Yabeda.tax_automations.rate_limit_remaining.set(tags, remaining) unless remaining.nil?
      # The header is an epoch; how long until the window opens is what a reader acts on.
      Yabeda.tax_automations.rate_limit_reset_seconds.set(tags, [reset_at - Time.current.to_i, 0].max) unless reset_at.nil?
    end

# The vendor refusals a send step answers rather than raises, since every attempt gets the
# same answer; any other client error goes to the retry ladder.
module TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::RefusalsHelper
  module_function

  TERMINAL_ERRORS = [
    TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::BaseClient::QuotaExceededError,
    TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::TokenRefreshable::InvalidGrantError,
    TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::BaseClient::UnauthorizedError,
    TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::BaseClient::ForbiddenError,
    TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::BaseClient::NotFoundError,
    TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::BaseClient::LockedError,
    TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::BaseClient::BadRequestError,
    TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::BaseClient::UnprocessableEntityError,
    TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::BaseClient::TargetIncompleteError,
    TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::BaseClient::TargetExpiredError,
    AbstractPolicy::PolicyError
  ].freeze

  # The refusals whose reason is not `api_error`.
  REASONS = {
    TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::BaseClient::QuotaExceededError => :exceeded,
    TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::BaseClient::InsufficientScopeError => :unauthorized,
    TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::TokenRefreshable::InvalidGrantError => :unauthorized,
    TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::BaseClient::UnauthorizedError => :unauthorized,
    AbstractPolicy::PolicyError => :forbidden
  }.freeze

  # Refusals the worker base answers, not the step: it kills the job and, for a grant, starts its verification.
  RAISED_ERRORS = [AbstractPolicy::PolicyError, TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::TokenRefreshable::InvalidGrantError].freeze

  # Refusals the vendor gives only when its contract or our configuration moved — a firm cannot lift them.
  REPORTED_ERRORS = [
    TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::BaseClient::InsufficientScopeError,
    TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::BaseClient::BadRequestError,
    TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::BaseClient::UnprocessableEntityError,
    TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::BaseClient::TargetIncompleteError
  ].freeze

  # @param error [StandardError] one of `TERMINAL_ERRORS`
  # @return [Symbol] one of `TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::Document::FAILURE_REASONS`
  def reason_for(error)
    error_class = REASONS.keys.find { |refusal_class| error.is_a?(refusal_class) }
    REASONS.fetch(error_class, :api_error)
  end

  # Ends the step's files under `reason_for(error)` — a system transition, scoped to the connection's firm since the
  # system passes every policy; the caller answers the refusal, and a policy refusal or a refused grant is raised on.
  #
  # @param error [StandardError] one of `TERMINAL_ERRORS`
  # @param tax_automation_documents [Array<TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::Document>]
  # @param connection [TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::HasOauthConnection]
  # @return [void]
  # @raise [AbstractPolicy::PolicyError] the refusal itself, once the files are ended
  def refuse!(error, tax_automation_documents, connection)
    reason = reason_for(error)

    report_refusal(error, tax_automation_documents, connection) if REPORTED_ERRORS.any? { |error_class| error.is_a?(error_class) }
    own_documents = Array(tax_automation_documents).select { |tax_automation_document| tax_automation_document.firm_id == connection.firm_id }
    system_actor = System.new
    TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::Documents::FailUpload.call(system_actor.user, system_actor, own_documents, reason)
    raise error if RAISED_ERRORS.any? { |error_class| error.is_a?(error_class) }
  end

  def report_refusal(error, tax_automation_documents, connection)
    tags = {error_context: Settings.product_clusters.tax_preparation, provider: tax_automation_documents.first.provider}
    contexts = {tax_automations: {connection_id: connection.id, tax_automation_document_ids: tax_automation_documents.map(&:id)}}

    ErrorReporter.report(error, tags, contexts)
  end
end

module TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::TokenRefreshable
  # The only door to the vendor API — nothing outside this module reads, checks
  # or renews a token.
  #
  # A withdrawal leaves the tokens in the row, so the state is the only thing
  # saying they must not be used: without the guard the client would go on
  # serving requests from a grant the firm took back, and the first renewal after
  # that would fail inside the state machine rather than here.
  #
  # @yieldparam access_token [String] a token verified as unexpired
  # @raise [InvalidGrantError] when the connection is in no state to carry a
  #   request — the firm has to authorize us again, which is what the error means
  #   everywhere else too
def with_access_token
    raise InvalidGrantError.new(I18n.t('invalid_grant', scope: I18N_ERRORS_SCOPE), connection: vendor_connection) unless vendor_connection.usable?

    refresh! unless vendor_connection.access_token_valid?

    yield vendor_connection.access_token
  end

class TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::BaseClient
  # @param headers [Hash] per-request headers on top of the authenticating ones
  # @yieldparam response [Faraday::Response] handed over in place of the parsed
  #   body when a vendor call assembles a value of its own from the answer — a
  #   pre-signed target is several of its fields at once, and reading them is the
  #   vendor's vocabulary rather than the transport's
  # @return [Hash] the parsed response body, or whatever the block makes of the
  #   whole response when one is given
def request(method_name, path, body: nil, params: nil, headers: {}, &block)
    Retry.retry_on(AUTH_ERRORS, AUTH_RETRIES_COUNT, timeout: AUTH_RETRY_TIMEOUT_SEC) do
      with_access_token do |access_token|
        # The renewal rides an operation of its own: its wait on the row lock says
        # nothing about how fast the vendor's API is.
        response = measured('api_request') { perform(method_name, path, access_token, body:, params:, headers:) }

        block ? block.call(response) : response.body
      end
    rescue UnauthorizedError => e
      # Counted on every attempt: a retried rejection is still a rejection, and a
      # metric that only sees the last one hides the ladder.
      track_failure('api_request', "HTTP_ERROR: #{e.code}")
      # The vendor refused a token whose stored expiry still reads valid, so the
      # next attempt has to carry one it minted rather than the one it just
      # rejected.
      refresh!(force: true)
      raise
    rescue ActiveRecord::LockWaitTimeout
      track_failure('api_request', 'LOCK_TIMEOUT')
      raise
    end
    # Both are retried together — waiting is the right answer to either — but
    # they leave differently. The 401 goes on as itself: it carries the vendor's
    # own account of the refusal, and every attempt is already counted, so it
    # must not fall through to the counting branch below. A lock timeout is not
    # an authorization failure at all and has nothing of the vendor to carry.
  rescue UnauthorizedError
    raise
  rescue ActiveRecord::LockWaitTimeout
    raise ConnectionBusyError, I18n.t('connection_busy', scope: I18N_ERRORS_SCOPE)
  rescue InvalidGrantError
    # The one failure retrying cannot help with, and the only one the firm has to
    # act on. Counted here because it reaches the caller through none of the
    # branches around it — the token module raises it in place of whatever the
    # vendor said.
    track_failure('api_request', 'INVALID_GRANT')
    raise
  rescue *NETWORK_ERRORS => e
    track_failure('api_request', "NETWORK_ERROR: #{e.class.name}")
    raise NetworkError, e.message
  rescue RequestError => e
    track_failure('api_request', "HTTP_ERROR: #{e.code}")
    raise
  end

module TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::TokenRefreshable
  # Suspected, not settled: `expired` keeps the row usable for the verification
  # whose exchange brings it back or `Connections::Renew` revokes.
  #
  # @raise [InvalidGrantError] always
def reject_grant!(message)
    vendor_connection.expire! if vendor_connection.may_expire?

    raise InvalidGrantError.new(message, connection: vendor_connection)
  end

module TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::TokenRefreshable
  # Renews under the row lock. The re-check inside the lock is what makes a
  # concurrent caller a waiter rather than a second refresher.
  #
  # @param force [Boolean] the vendor rejected the token we hold, so its stored
  #   expiry says nothing — renewing is right unless another caller has already
  #   replaced that very token.
def refresh!(force: false)
    reject_grant!(I18n.t('invalid_grant', scope: I18N_ERRORS_SCOPE)) unless vendor_connection.refresh_token_valid?

    rejected_token = vendor_connection.access_token if force

    # On its own DB connection, so the write outlives a rollback of the caller's
    # transaction. The vendor has already rotated the refresh token by then, and
    # a rolled-back row keeps a token the vendor no longer honours — the grant is
    # dead with no way back.
    ThreadHelper.run_in_new_thread do
      Thread.current.report_on_exception = false

      vendor_connection.transaction(requires_new: true) do
        # Bounds the wait when the caller's own transaction already holds this
        # row: what would be a deadlock against the thread above surfaces as a
        # LockWaitTimeout the client retries.
        ActiveRecord::Base.connection.execute("SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '#{CONNECTION_LOCK_TIMEOUT_SEC}s'")

        vendor_connection.with_lock do
          # The guard at the door read the row as it stood when the request began;
          # this reads it as it stands now. A withdrawal that landed while we
          # queued behind the lock leaves a row the transition below does not lead
          # out of, and the caller is owed the same error as any other dead grant.
          raise InvalidGrantError.new(I18n.t('invalid_grant', scope: I18N_ERRORS_SCOPE), connection: vendor_connection) unless vendor_connection.may_refresh?

          # Whoever held the lock before us may have renewed already, and what
          # counts as "already" depends on what sent us here: preemptively any
          # unexpired token will do, but after a rejection only one that is no
          # longer the token the vendor turned down.
          next if force && vendor_connection.access_token != rejected_token
          next if !force && vendor_connection.access_token_valid?

          vendor_connection.store_tokens!(**refresh_tokens!)
          # The exchange settles the grant's standing in both directions, so the
          # transition follows it either way: here it stamps `refreshed_at` and
          # brings an expired grant back to connected, and in {#reject_grant!} it
          # moves a refused one further out.
          vendor_connection.refresh!
        end
      end
    end
    # Named in full because the exchange reaches the token endpoint through the
    # including client's error middleware — the one place this module knows it is
    # mixed into exactly one class.
  rescue TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::BaseClient::RequestError => e
    raise unless grant_refused?(e)

    reject_grant!(e.message)
  end

# Shared setup for tax automation vendor client specs. Lives here rather than in
# the specs so the next vendor reuses the contract check instead of copying it.
module TaxAutomationsHelpers
  INSTEAD_CONTRACT_PATH = 'specs/TD-95046-instead-integration/contracts/instead_openapi_spec.yml'
  INSTEAD_FIXTURES_PATH = 'spec/fixtures/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead'

  # A Faraday test-stub reply carrying a JSON body. Deliberately keyword-free:
  # with an optional kwarg, Ruby parses `json_response('Key' => 1)` as keyword
  # arguments rather than as the positional hash the caller means.
  def json_response(body)
    [200, {'Content-Type' => 'application/json'}, body.to_json]
  end

  # The stand-in endpoint the base-client spec drives its subclass through.
  def stub_vendor_ping(status:, body: nil, headers: {'Content-Type' => 'application/json'})
    transport.get('/ping') { [status, headers, body] }
  end

  # The vendor's token endpoint answering nothing: what a renewal sees during an
  # outage, before the client's own timeout gives up on it.
  def stub_instead_token_endpoint_down
    stub_request(:post, "#{TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::Instead::Client::BASE_URL}/oauth2/token").to_timeout
  end

  def instead_fixture(name)
    JSON.parse(Rails.root.join(INSTEAD_FIXTURES_PATH, "#{name}.json").read)
  end

  # The body Instead refuses a request with — `instead_error('NOT_FOUND_DOCUMENT', 'Not found - Document not found.')`.
  def instead_error(identifier, message, parameters = nil)
    {'Error' => {'Identifier' => identifier, 'Message' => message, 'Parameters' => parameters}.compact}
  end

  def instead_started_upload(file_uuid)
    upload = instead_fixture('start_upload')
    upload['FileUUID'] = file_uuid
    upload['Upload']['ExpiresAt'] = 10.minutes.from_now.iso8601

    {status: 201, body: upload.to_json, headers: {'Content-Type' => 'application/json'}}
  end

  def stub_instead_send(file_uuids:, size:)
    base_url = TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::Instead::Client::BASE_URL
    bucket_url = instead_fixture('start_upload').dig('Upload', 'URL')
    started_uploads = file_uuids.map { |file_uuid| instead_started_upload(file_uuid) }

    stub_request(:post, "#{base_url}/entities").to_return_json(status: 201, body: {'Entity' => instead_fixture('entity').merge('EntityType' => 'INDIVIDUAL')})
    stub_request(:post, "#{base_url}/docs/uploads").to_return(*started_uploads)
    stub_request(:post, bucket_url).to_return(status: 204)
    file_uuids.each do |file_uuid|
      stub_request(:put, "#{base_url}/docs/#{file_uuid}").to_return_json(status: 200, body: {'File' => instead_fixture('file').merge('UUID' => file_uuid, 'Size' => size)})
    end
  end

  # One answer per page, in order — `{'Files' => [...], 'NextPageToken' => ...}`.
  def stub_instead_list_docs(*pages)
    responses = pages.map { |page| {status: 200, body: page} }

    stub_request(:post, "#{TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::Instead::Client::BASE_URL}/docs").to_return_json(*responses)
  end

  # One answer per page, in order — `{'Entities' => [...], 'NextPageToken' => ...}`; an empty listing by default,
  # which is what a connect starts the entity sync against.
  def stub_instead_list_entities(*pages)
    responses = pages.presence || [{'Entities' => []}]
    responses = responses.map { |page| {status: 200, body: page} }

    stub_request(:get, "#{TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::Instead::Client::BASE_URL}/entities").with(query: hash_including({})).to_return_json(*responses)
  end

  # A UUIDv7 minted at `time`, the shape Instead gives a delivery's `id`.
  def instead_event_id(time)
    hex = format('%012x', (time.to_r * 1000).to_i) + SecureRandom.hex(10)
    hex[12] = '7'

    "#{hex[0, 8]}-#{hex[8, 4]}-#{hex[12, 4]}-#{hex[16, 4]}-#{hex[20, 12]}"
  end

  def stub_instead_get_doc_not_found(file_uuid)
    stub_request(:get, "#{TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::Instead::Client::BASE_URL}/docs/#{file_uuid}").to_return_json(status: 404, body: instead_error('NOT_FOUND_DOCUMENT', 'Not found - Document not found.'))
  end

  def instead_contract
    @instead_contract ||= YAML.load_file(Rails.root.join(INSTEAD_CONTRACT_PATH))
  end

  # Validates a payload against a named component schema of the vendor contract.
  # The whole document goes in as the schema root so internal `$ref`s resolve.
  def conforms_to_contract?(schema_name, payload)
    JSON::Validator.validate(instead_contract.merge('$ref' => "#/components/schemas/#{schema_name}"), payload)
  end
end

      # contact_custom_fields), and `account_full_name` (non-nil only when the
      # contact has exactly one undeleted linked client).
      #

      # — existence non-disclosure (SC-005; docs/crm/public_api.md:47,70).
      #

      # parity with the pre-TD-87986 master behavior of this shared lookup. The
      # SMS-campaign caller still rejects soft-deleted recipients downstream via
      # `Communication::Api::ContactPhoneNumbers.list_by_contact`. Whether this
      # Public API should filter soft-deleted is a CRM-domain decision tracked
      # separately, not folded into the SMS cross-cluster cleanup.
def find(firm:, user:, actor:, contact_id:)
        result = Crm::Contacts::Find.call(user, actor, firm, contact_id)

        if result.successful?
          {success: true, errors: {}, data: contact_data(result.data)}
        else
          {success: false, errors: result.errors, reason: :not_authorized, data: nil}
        end
      end

def list_by_account(firm:, user:, actor:, account_id:)
        result = Crm::Contacts::ListByAccount.call(user, actor, firm, account_id)

        contacts = result.data.map do |row|
          {
            contact_id: row[:id],
            phone:      row[:phone],
            name:       row[:name]

        end

        {success: true, errors: {}, data: {contacts: contacts}}
